object_description: lateral volume parallel to the street with a staircase-like descending classroom wing
design_condition: a structure aligned parallel to the street forms a lateral end to the complex at a respectful distance from the existing building, and its stepped classroom wing bridges the two levels of the topography

positive: The new structure forms a lateral end to the complex while keeping a respectful distance from the existing building
It creates a connection between the two levels of the site
An esplanade between old and new building offers a view of the expansive landscape, a great quality of the chosen placement
The staircase-like arrangement of classrooms creates a natural transition to the uses on the lower level
The classroom wing oscillates in an interesting way between building structure and designed landscape, giving surprising spaciousness
The resulting outdoor spaces work as break areas, outdoor classrooms and a grandstand for varied activities
A second spatial centre on the lower level gives the additional uses an independent address
The upper playground becomes part of a sequence of open spaces stretching from the village to the landscape
The open space design impresses with clear zoning and differentiation in close dialogue with the school rooms
Paths and shortcuts create a high degree of permeability and embed the complex in the existing network
The library facing the large playground forms an appropriate prelude to the childcare building
The kindergartens are appropriately organised with a direct exit to the outdoor space visible from the classrooms
The direct arrangement of assembly hall next to the gymnasium generates interesting synergies
The very harmonious positioning of the new volumes is impressive from a heritage point of view
The prominent entrance situation on the lower level could compensate for deficits of the existing entrance
The positioning of the volumes limits excavation volumes and excavation securing costs
A sensible phasing can be derived from the division of uses
From the challenging topography the authors generate an exciting architectural theme connecting the levels naturally
negative: The rows of trees on the upper level and the street space are not convincing
Dividing the childcare rooms over three storeys is not convincing
Long and narrow corridors, dark for long stretches, connect the rooms
The small studio zones degenerate into work niches
The outdoor play areas lie directly in front of the classrooms, which is not ideal
Accessing classrooms from outside through the group rooms considerably restricts their usability
Flexibility between rooms, group rooms and studio areas is impaired by the position of checkrooms, WCs and entrances
The architectural relationship between childcare building and classroom wing remains unclear
The exclusive northern orientation of the classrooms is viewed critically, worsened by the large canopy reducing light
The chosen spacing of the gymnasium ceiling beams seems too large
The bracing concept is not clearly shown in the plans
The floor plans are not convincing over long stretches
